**Finding submitted: deviation (Rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What the document does:** Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and "all Intellectual Property Rights therein" in Licensor, with "Intellectual Property Rights" (1.6) defined only as Licensor's rights and "Derivative Work" (1.3) capturing "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology."
- **Why it fails the fallback:** The bespoke customization / unique client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087) falls within Licensor's ownership with no assignment and no licence back — only the limited non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence, which terminates with the Agreement and triggers a return-of-materials obligation (Article XXI). There is also no Customer Data ownership provision anywhere; Confidential Information (1.2) protects only information disclosed *to* Licensee, so our trading, order, client and account data is unaddressed.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** a "Notwithstanding the foregoing" carve-out inserted after Article III confirming (i) we retain all rights in Licensee Data and our IP, (ii) paid-for deliverables are assigned to us with Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP and granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for materials embedded in those deliverables, and (iii) no joint ownership is created. The comment offers the fallback (perpetual licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables) if Licensor resists assignment.
- Licensor's retention of the platform itself is not challenged.
